description: SchemaConverter $ref inlining: sibling keys written beside a `$ref` node MUST survive resolution, with the sibling winning over the resolved `$defs` entry on key conflict. Exercises the converter's ref-resolution step in isolation, called with strict=false so additionalProperties injection (a separate, already-pinned concern) does not add noise to the expected output. Added because apcore 0.31.0 (decision D-124/D-98) and apcore-toolkit 0.12.0 fixed the identical defect in their own `$ref` resolvers — this bridge's schema.py/.rs/.ts `_inline_refs`/`inline_refs`/`_inlineRefs` is an independent implementation that had the same bug: `{"$ref": "#/$defs/X", "x-sensitive": true}` discarded `x-sensitive` entirely, which is a credential-disclosure path because the router's output redaction (see output_redaction.json) reads `x-sensitive` off the RESOLVED schema to decide what to mask.
entry_point: SchemaConverter.convert_input_schema(descriptor, strict=false) — exercises the private ref-resolution step (Python: SchemaConverter._inline_refs; TypeScript: SchemaConverter._inlineRefs; Rust: SchemaConverter::inline_refs) via the public strict=false path so drivers do not need private-method access.

test_cases.description: The pre-fix behaviour is unchanged when a $ref has no siblings. Regression guard: the merge must not perturb the ordinary case.
A schema with no $ref anywhere is returned structurally unchanged.

THE SECURITY CASE. `x-sensitive` written beside a $ref survives resolution. The router's output redaction reads x-sensitive off the resolved output_schema; dropping it here means a sensitive field behind a $ref reaches the redactor with nothing to mask on and is returned in plaintext. Mirrors apcore-toolkit 0.12.0's ref_resolution.json#ref_resolution_003 and apcore 0.31.0's D-98.
The merge is NOT limited to `x-` extension keys. Restricting it to the one symptom that was noticed would leave `description`, `title` and `deprecated` silently dropped.
On a key present in both, the SIBLING wins — it is the more specific, author-written value. The $defs entry is the default; the sibling is the override.
A sibling carrying its own nested $ref is walked like any other subtree — the merge does not smuggle unresolved references past the resolver.
The rule applies at every depth, not only at the schema root — this is the shape a real tool input actually produces, where the marked field is a nested property.
When a $ref resolves to another $ref, siblings contributed at each hop all survive, with the outermost winning on conflict — the same precedence as a single hop, applied transitively.

error_cases.description: This fix changes what happens to siblings on a RESOLVED $ref only. A $ref pointing at a name absent from $defs must keep raising, unchanged — sibling merging is not a substitute for a real definition.
